title.en: Always Believe in Yourself: a poem by Dorothy Hewitt
A poem that speaks to you directly

text.en: Imagine a friend putting a hand on your shoulder and telling you that you have everything you need. This poem does that.

Believe in Yourself is a poem by Dorothy Hewitt. It speaks directly to the reader in the form of advice.
The opening instruction is to always believe in yourself, not to limit yourself, and to be kind to yourself.
The poem repeats the word always. This repetition emphasises that confidence must be steady.
It reminds us that we already have the intelligence and ability we need, so we can reach what we are after, even if it does not come the way we expect.
When we are tested beyond our endurance, the poem advises us to continue, persist and hold on to courage.
It asks us to let laughter and encouragement surround us, so a positive circle of people helps us grow.
The last lines advise thinking big and keeping hands and heart open so we can receive all of life's gifts. Open hands and heart are a metaphor for being ready for life.
The poem is in free verse and uses the imperative, a form of verb that gives a command or advice. The tone is encouraging and the theme is self-belief with persistence.

problem.en: Pick out the imperative advice in the poem and say what it teaches.

prompt.en: How does the poem help a reader who feels like giving up?

requiredIdeas.en: You already have the ability you need
Persist and hold on to courage
Encouragement and an open heart bring gifts

points.en: Believe in Yourself is an encouraging poem by Dorothy Hewitt.
It uses imperative lines and repetition.
It advises persistence, courage and an open heart.
Its theme is self-belief with perseverance.
